$$ \frac{\partial\overline{\eta}_{S}}{\partial(\tau_{e}Z_{e})}=\bigg[\sum_{e\in[E]}\varpi_{e}(\Sigma_{e})_{S,S}\bigg]^{-1}\varpi_{e}(\Sigma_{e}^{1/2})_{S,\cdot}. $$

Thus from the second line of Equation (6), we know

$$ \overline{\delta}_{e}^{{(p)}}=\varpi_{e}\cdot\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\bigg(\bigg[\sum_{e\in[E]}\varpi_{e}(\Sigma_{e})_{S,S}\bigg]^{-1}(\Sigma_{e})_{S,S}\bigg)\right], $$

thus proving the third line of Equation (6).

We are left to prove $\lim_{p}\overline{\delta}_{e}^{(p)}=\overline{\delta}_{e}$ . We know from Assumption 3(c) that

By the third line of Equation (6), $\sum_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}^{(p)}=\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\lvert S\rvert]=\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\lVert\overline{\eta}\rVert_{0}]$ . As $p\to\infty$ , we know $\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\lVert\overline{\eta}\rVert_{0}]=\sum_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}$ . This completes the proof of Proposition 1.

Under Assumptions 2,3,4, and Definitions C.1,C.2, $\forall\,\epsilon>0$ , $\exists\,T=T(\epsilon)$ . s.t. $\forall\,j>i\geq T$ , $\forall e\in[E]$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\lim_{p\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\left[\frac{1}{p}\left\lVert v_{e}^{j}-v_{e}^{i}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq\epsilon\right]=1,\quad \displaystyle\lim_{p\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\left[\frac{1}{n_{e}}\left\lVert r_{e}^{j}-r_{e}^{i}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq\epsilon\right]=1, \displaystyle\lim_{p\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\bigg[\frac{1}{p}\left\lVert\eta^{j}-\eta^{i}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq\epsilon\bigg]=1,\quad \displaystyle\max_{e\in[E]}\{1-\rho_{e}^{i,j}\}\leq\epsilon. $$

Lemma C.3 is proved in Section C.1.3.

#### Lemma C.4 (Sub-Gradient Going to Zero).

Under Assumptions 2,3,4, and Definitions C.1,C.2, define a vector $s^{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{p}$ by

$$ s^{t}=\frac{1}{\theta^{*}}\left[\diag(\vec{\lambda})^{-1}\right]\sum_{e\in[E]}\varpi_{e}^{*}\left(\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}v_{e}^{t}+\Sigma_{e}(\beta_{e}-\eta^{t})\right). $$

Then $s^{t}\in\partial\lVert\eta^{t}\rVert_{1}$ . Moreover, if we define $\nabla L(\eta^{t})=-\sum_{e\in[E]}\pi_{e}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}}(y_{e}-{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\eta^{t})+\lambda s^{t}$ as a sub-gradient of $L$ defined in Equation (2), then $\forall\,\epsilon>0$ , $\exists\,T$ s.t. $\forall\,t\geq T$ , $\lim_{p}\mathbb{P}\left[\frac{1}{p}\lVert\nabla L(\eta^{t})\rVert_{2}^{2}<\epsilon\right]=1$ .

Lemma C.4 is proved in Section C.1.4.

#### Lemma C.5 (Bounding the Sub-Gradient’s Magnitude).

For any constant $c\in(0,1)$ , define $S^{t}(c)=\{j\in[p]:\lvert s^{t}_{j}\rvert\geq 1-c\}$ where $s^{t}$ has been defined in Equation (C-14). Under Assumptions 2,3,4, and Definitions C.1,C.2, for any $\epsilon>0$ , there exists $c=c(\epsilon)\in(0,1)$ invariant to the time step $t$ s.t. for any time step $t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ , we have $\lim_{p}\mathbb{P}\left[\lvert S^{t}(c)\rvert/p\leq\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}+\epsilon\right]=1$ .

Lemma C.5 is proved in Section C.1.5.

#### Lemma C.6.

Under Assumptions 2,3,4, and Definitions C.1,C.2, for any $\epsilon>0$ , $\exists\,T$ s.t. $\forall\,t\geq T$ , $\lim_{p}\mathbb{P}\left[\frac{1}{p}\lVert\eta^{t}-\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}<\epsilon\right]=1$ .

Lemma C.6 is proved in Section C.1.6.

#### Proof of Theorem 2.

We work with small $\epsilon$ and $t\geq T$ required by Lemma C.6. By Lemma C.1 and Lemma C.2, we have $\lim_{p}\mathbb{P}\left[\max\{\frac{1}{p}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2},\frac{1}{p}\lVert\eta^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2}\}\leq M\right]=1$ . By Assumption 2(c), we can choose $M$ large enough s.t. $\limsup_{p}\frac{1}{p}\lVert\beta_{e}\rVert_{2}^{2}<M\ \forall\,e\in[E]$ as well. So we can choose $\epsilon$ small enough s.t. with probability approaching $1$ as $p\to\infty$ at a fixed $t$ , for any sequence of order- $k$ pseudo-Lipschitz functions $\phi:(\mathbb{R}^{p})^{E+1}\to\mathbb{R}$ $(k\geq 1)$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\left\lvert\phi(\eta^{t},\beta_{1},\cdots,\beta_{E})-\phi(\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}},\beta_{1},\cdots,\beta_{E})\right\rvert \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle L\left[1+\sum_{e\in[E]}\left(\frac{\lVert\beta_{e}\rVert_{2}}{\sqrt{p}}\right)^{k-1}+\left(\frac{\lVert\eta^{t}\rVert_{2}}{\sqrt{p}}\right)^{k-1}+\left(\frac{\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}}{\sqrt{p}}\right)^{k-1}\right]\frac{\lVert\eta^{t}-\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}}{\sqrt{p}}\leq\frac{\epsilon}{2}. $$

Also with probability going to 1 as $p\to\infty$ , we have $\lvert\phi(\eta^{t},\beta_{1},\cdots,\beta_{E})-\mathbb{E}\left[\phi(\overline{\eta},\beta_{1},\cdots,\beta_{E})\right]\rvert<\epsilon/2$ by Lemma C.2. Thus for any small enough $\epsilon$ , we have $\lvert\phi(\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}},\beta_{1},\cdots,\beta_{E})-\mathbb{E}\left[\phi(\overline{\eta},\beta_{1},\cdots,\beta_{E})\right]\rvert<\epsilon$ with probability going to 1 as $p\to\infty$ . This proves Theorem 2. ∎

### C.1 Proof of Auxiliary Lemmas in Section C

#### C.1.1 Proof of Lemma C.1

The proof follows the same steps as those of Lemma 3.2, Bayati and Montanari [32]. First of all,

$$ \displaystyle\limsup_{p}L(\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}})/p\leq\limsup_{p}L(0)/p\leq\sum_{e\in[E]}\pi_{e}\cdot\frac{\lVert y_{e}\rVert_{2}^{2}}{2p}\leq\sum_{e\in[E]}\pi_{e}\cdot\left[\frac{\lVert w_{e}\rVert_{2}^{2}}{p}+\frac{\sigma_{\max}({X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}})^{2}c_{1}^{2}\lVert\beta_{e}\rVert_{2}^{2}}{p}\right]. $$

By Lemma F.4, $\lim_{p}\sigma_{\max}({X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}})=1+\sqrt{\kappa_{e}},a.s.$ . By Assumption 2, we know $\limsup_{p}L(\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}})/p<+\infty$ . Now if $\kappa_{e}<1$ for any $e:\pi_{e}>0$ , then we know $\liminf_{p}\sigma_{\min}({X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2})\geq(1-\sqrt{\kappa_{e}})/c_{1}^{1/2}>0$ by Lemma F.4 and Assumption 2, and thus $\frac{1}{p}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq B_{1}\cdot\frac{1}{p}\lVert{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}\ a.s.$ for some constant $B_{1}>c_{1}/(1-\sqrt{\kappa_{e}})^{2}$ as $p\to\infty$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\lVert{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq\frac{2}{p}\left[\lVert y_{e}-{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}+\lVert y_{e}\rVert_{2}^{2}\right]\leq\frac{2}{\pi_{e}}\left[\frac{L(\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}})}{p}+\frac{L(0)}{p}\right], $$

and we have proved Lemma C.1. From now on, we focus on the the case of $\kappa_{e}\geq 1$ for all the environments $e:\pi_{e}>0$ .

For any $e:\pi_{e}>0$ , let $P_{e}^{\|}$ be the projection matrix onto $\mathrm{\ker}({X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2})$ and $P_{e}^{\bot}$ onto $\mathrm{\ker}({X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2})^{\bot}$ . Then $\frac{1}{p}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq\frac{1}{p}\lVert P_{e}^{\|}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}+\frac{1}{p}\lVert P_{e}^{\bot}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}$ . At any finite $p$ , $\mathrm{\ker}({X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2})$ is still a uniformly random space, so Kashin’s theorem (c.f. Lemma F.5) applies just like in the proof of Lemma 3.2, Bayati and Montanari [32]. For some constant $B_{1}$ , the relationship below holds almost surely as $p\to\infty$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq B_{1}\left(\frac{1}{p}\lVert P_{e}^{\|}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{1}\right)^{2}+\frac{1}{p}\lVert P_{e}^{\bot}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq 2B_{1}\left(\frac{1}{p}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{1}\right)^{2}+\frac{2B_{1}+1}{p}\lVert P_{e}^{\bot}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}. $$

The first inequality in the above line uses Kashin’s theorem, and the second has omitted some details because they are the same as those in Bayati and Montanari [32]. For the former term, $\limsup_{p}\frac{1}{p}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{1}<+\infty,a.s.$ because $\limsup_{p}\frac{1}{p}L(\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}})<+\infty$ . For the latter term, since $\mathrm{\ker}({X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2})^{\bot}=\mathrm{range}(\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}})$ , $P_{e}^{\bot}=\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}}({X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}})^{-1}{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}$ . By Lemma F.4 and Assumption 2, there exists $B_{2}>0$ s.t.

$$ \lVert P_{e}^{\bot}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}\leq B_{2}\lVert{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}P_{e}^{\bot}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}=B_{2}\lVert{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2},a.s., $$

and $\lVert{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}$ has been bounded by Equation (C-15). Now we have shown $\limsup_{p}\frac{1}{p}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}<+\infty$ .

#### C.1.2 Proof of Lemma C.2

#### Proof of Lemma C.2.

The way to prove Lemma C.2 is to show the GLAMP instance defined in Definition C.1 is a legitimate multi-environment GLAMP as defined in Definition 2. However, we are faced with one more technicality: we have used external randomness to initialize the iterates. As a result, the original GLAMP would give results conditioning on a realization of $\eta^{0}$ , which is not exactly Lemma C.2.

We use a sub-sequence argument to address this technicality. We know from Lemma F.2 and Assumption 3 that, ( $\overline{\eta}=\overline{\eta}(\tau_{1}^{*},\tau_{2}^{*},\cdots,\tau_{E}^{*})$ )

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\eta^{0}= \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}\right]+o_{\mathsf{P}}(1) \displaystyle\implies\mathop{\mathrm{plim}}_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\eta^{0}=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}\right], \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}(\eta^{0})^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\eta^{0}= \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\overline{\eta}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}\right]+o_{\mathsf{P}}(1) \displaystyle\implies\mathop{\mathrm{plim}}_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}(\eta^{0})^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\eta^{0}=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\overline{\eta}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}\right], \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}(\eta^{0})^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\mathbb{E}[\overline{\eta}]= \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\overline{\eta}_{(1)}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}_{(2)}\right]+o_{\mathsf{P}}(1) \displaystyle\implies\mathop{\mathrm{plim}}_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}(\eta^{0})^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\mathbb{E}[\overline{\eta}]=\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\overline{\eta}_{(1)}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}_{(2)}\right], $$

where in the last line, $\overline{\eta}_{(1)}$ and $\overline{\eta}_{(2)}$ are mutually independent copies of $\overline{\eta}$ . The existence of the limit $\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\overline{\eta}_{(1)}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}_{(2)}\right]$ is implied by $\lim_{p}H^{{(p)}}=H$ in Assumption 4(b) combined with Assumption 3(b).

Recall that a sequence of random variables converges in probability iff any of its sub-sequences admit a further sub-sequence that converges almost surely. If we prove Lemma C.2 along any sub-sequence of $(p,n_{1},n_{2},\cdots,n_{E})$ on which the three limits involving $\eta^{0}$ in Equation (C-16) all hold almost surely (instead of merely in probability), we will have proved Lemma C.2 itself. This is because any sub-sequence of $(p,n_{1},n_{2},\cdots,n_{E})$ firstly admits a further sub-sequence along which all the limits in Equation (C-16) hold almost surely. If we prove the desired convergence in Lemma C.2 along the further sub-sequence, we will have proved Lemma C.2 itself, since the limit is free of the choice of specific sub-sequences.

With a slight abuse of notation, we still use letters $(p,n_{1},n_{2},\cdots,n_{E})$ to denote the sub-sequence along with the three limits involving $\eta^{0}$ in Equation (C-16) all hold almost surely.

We specify a GLAMP instance in the following way: Let $\{q_{e}:e\in[E]\}$ all be sufficiently large and fixed integers. Let $B=[\beta_{1}|\beta_{2}|\cdots|\beta_{E}|\eta^{0}|0|0|\cdots]\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}$ , $W_{e}=[w_{e}|0|0|\cdots]\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{e}\times q}$ . At any time step $t\in\mathbb{N}$ , $\forall\,e\in[E]$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\ V_{e}^{t}= \displaystyle\left[v_{e}^{1}|v_{e}^{2}|\cdots|v_{e}^{t}|0|0|\cdots\right], \displaystyle\eta_{e}^{t}(V_{1}^{t},\cdots,V_{E}^{t})= \displaystyle\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\left[\beta_{e}|\eta^{0}|\eta(v_{1}^{1},\cdots,v_{E}^{1})|\eta(v_{1}^{2},\cdots,v_{E}^{2})|\cdots|\eta(v_{1}^{t},\cdots,v_{E}^{t})|0|0|\cdots\right], \displaystyle R_{e}^{t}= \displaystyle\left[{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\beta_{e}|r_{e}^{0}|r_{e}^{1}|\cdots|r_{e}^{t}|0|0|\cdots\right], \displaystyle\Psi_{e}^{t}(R_{e}^{t})= \displaystyle\kappa_{e}\left[y_{e}-r_{e}^{0}|y_{e}-r_{e}^{1}|\cdots|y_{e}-r_{e}^{t}|0|0|\cdots\right]\quad(y_{e}={X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\beta_{e}+w_{e}). $$

The GLAMP instance starts from $V_{e}^{0}=0,\ \forall\,e\in[E]$ .

Now we know the GLAMP iterates take the form

$$ \displaystyle v_{e}^{t}= \displaystyle{\displaystyle X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}}(y_{e}-r_{e}^{t-1})-\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\beta_{e}+\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\eta(v_{1}^{t-1},v_{2}^{t-1},\cdots,v_{E}^{t-1}), \displaystyle r_{e}^{t}= \displaystyle{\displaystyle X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\eta(v_{1}^{t},v_{2}^{t},\cdots,v_{E}^{t})-\kappa_{e}(y_{e}-r_{e}^{t-1})\cdot\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\left(\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\frac{\partial\eta}{\partial v_{e}^{t}}(Z_{1}^{t},Z_{2}^{t},\cdots,Z_{E}^{t})\right)\right]. $$

where the Gaussian variables used are yet to be characterized by the state evolution.

To fully write out its form, we need the state evolution first. We discard the all-zero columns in $V_{e}^{t}$ and $R_{e}^{t}$ , start from $\Sigma_{(R,e)}^{0}$ and compute the first two matrices for the state evolution. From there, we prove the whole state evolution for $V^{t}_{e}$ with induction.

- 1. $\Sigma_{(R,e)}^{0}=\begin{bmatrix}\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\beta_{e}&\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}]\\ \lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}]&\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\overline{\eta}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}]\\ \end{bmatrix}$ .

- 2. $\Sigma_{(V,e)}^{1}=\lim_{p}\frac{1}{n_{e}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert w_{e}+(Z_{(R,e)}^{0})_{1}-(Z_{(R,e)}^{0})_{2}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right]$ where $Z^{0}_{(R,e)}=[(Z_{(R,e)}^{0})_{1}|(Z_{(R,e)}^{0})_{2}]\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times 2}$ has iid rows drawn from $\mathcal{N}(0,\kappa_{e}\Sigma_{(R,e)}^{0})$ . Simplifying it with Assumption 3 and 4, $\Sigma_{(V,e)}^{1}=\mathbb{E}[W_{e}^{2}]+\kappa_{e}\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\lVert\overline{\eta}-\beta_{e}\rVert_{\Sigma_{e}}^{2}]=(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}$ .

- 3. $\Sigma_{(R,e)}^{1}=\begin{bmatrix}\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\beta_{e}&\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}]&\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}]\\ \lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}]&\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\overline{\eta}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}]&\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\overline{\eta}_{(1)}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}_{(2)}\right]\\ \lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}]&\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\overline{\eta}_{(1)}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}_{(2)}\right]&\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\overline{\eta}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}],\end{bmatrix}$ where $\overline{\eta}_{(1)}$ and $\overline{\eta}_{(2)}$ are mutually independent copies of $\overline{\eta}$ .

- 4. $\Sigma_{(V,e)}^{2}=\begin{bmatrix}(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}&(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}H_{e}(\vec{0}_{E})\\ (\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}H_{e}(\vec{0}_{E})&(\tau_{E}^{*})^{2}\\ \end{bmatrix}$ . For the diagnoal elements of $\Sigma_{(V,e)}^{2}$ we have simplified it in the same way as $\Sigma_{(V,e)}^{1}$ . For the off-diagonal term, it is $\displaystyle\lim_{p}\frac{1}{n_{e}}\mathbb{E}\left[(w_{e}+(Z_{(R,e)}^{0})_{1}-(Z_{(R,e)}^{0})_{2})^{{\top}}(w_{e}+(Z_{(R,e)}^{0})_{1}-(Z_{(R,e)}^{0})_{3})\right]$ $\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[W_{e}^{2}]+\kappa_{e}\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[(\overline{\eta}_{(1)}-\beta_{e})^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}(\overline{\eta}_{(2)}-\beta_{e})\right]=(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}H_{e}(\vec{0}_{E}),$ where $\overline{\eta}_{(1)}$ and $\overline{\eta}_{(2)}$ are mutually independent copies of $\overline{\eta}$ .

where $\overline{\eta}_{(1)}$ and $\overline{\eta}_{(2)}$ are mutually independent copies of $\overline{\eta}$ .

$$ \displaystyle(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}\rho_{e}^{i,t+1}= \displaystyle\lim_{p}\frac{1}{n_{e}}\mathbb{E}\left[(w_{e}+(Z_{(R,e)}^{t})_{1}-(Z_{(R,e)}^{t})_{i+1})^{{\top}}(w_{e}+(Z_{(R,e)}^{t})_{1}-(Z_{(R,e)}^{t})_{t+2})\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[W_{e}^{2}]+\kappa_{e}\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[({\eta}(Z^{i-1})-\beta_{e})^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}({\eta}(Z^{t})-\beta_{e})\right], $$

where $Z^{i-1}=[Z^{i-1}_{1}|Z^{i-1}_{2}|\cdots|Z^{i-1}_{E}]$ and $Z^{t}=[Z^{t}_{1}|Z^{t}_{2}|\cdots|Z^{t}_{E}]$ , $\{(Z_{e}^{i-1},Z_{e}^{t}):e\in[E]\}$ are $E$ independent random tuples, and each row of $[Z^{i-1}_{e}|Z^{t}_{e}]$ is sampled iid from $\mathcal{N}(0,(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}[1,\rho_{e}^{i-1,t};\rho_{e}^{i-1,t},1])$ . Thus $\rho_{e}^{1,t+1}=H_{e}(\rho^{i-1,t})$ .

Now we have verified the GLAMP iterates take the form of Definition C.1 and their state evolution is described by Definition C.2. By GLAMP convergence, we have shown Lemma C.2. ∎

#### C.1.3 Proof of Lemma C.3

We first prove a lemma and then use it to prove Lemma C.3.

#### Lemma C.7.

For the function $H$ defined in Assumption 4(b) and any $e\in[E]$ , its $e$ -th element $H_{e}=H_{e}(\rho_{1},\cdots,\rho_{E})$ is increasing and strictly convex in $\rho_{i}$ , $\forall\,i\in[E]$ , while we fix $\{\rho_{j}:j\neq i\}$ . We have

$$ 0\leq\frac{\partial H_{e}}{\partial\rho_{i}}\leq\frac{\kappa_{e}(\tau_{i}^{*})^{2}\varpi_{i}^{*}}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}\varpi^{*}_{e}}\overline{\delta}_{i}\overline{\delta}_{e}. $$

#### Proof of Lemma C.7.

The first half of Proposition C.7 follows the same argument as that of Lemma C.1 of Bayati and Montanari [32], or Lemma C.2 of Donoho and Montanari [33]. To elaborate, we first assume without loss of generality that $i=1$ . We represent the function $H_{e}$ in an alternative way. Let $H_{e}=\lim_{p}H^{{(p)}}_{e}$ , where $H^{{(p)}}_{e}$ is the finite- $p$ version of the same function, i.e.

$$ \displaystyle H_{e}^{{(p)}}(\rho_{1},\rho_{2},\cdots,\rho_{E})= \displaystyle\frac{1}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}}\left\{\mathbb{E}[W_{e}^{2}]+\kappa_{e}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[(\overline{\eta}_{{(1)}}-\beta_{e})^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}(\overline{\eta}_{{(2)}}-\beta_{e})\right]\right\} \displaystyle\mathrm{where}\ \overline{\eta}_{{(1)}}= \displaystyle\eta(\tau^{*}_{1}\sqrt{\rho_{1}}Z_{1}+\tau_{1}^{*}\sqrt{1-\rho_{1}}Y_{1},\tau^{*}_{2}\sqrt{\rho_{2}}Z_{2}+\tau_{2}^{*}\sqrt{1-\rho_{2}}Y_{2},\cdots,\tau^{*}_{E}\sqrt{\rho_{E}}Z_{E}+\tau_{E}^{*}\sqrt{1-\rho_{E}}Y_{E}), \displaystyle\overline{\eta}_{{(2)}}= \displaystyle\eta(\tau^{*}_{1}\sqrt{\rho_{1}}Z_{1}+\tau_{1}^{*}\sqrt{1-\rho_{1}}Y_{1}^{\prime},\tau^{*}_{2}\sqrt{\rho_{2}}Z_{2}+\tau_{2}^{*}\sqrt{1-\rho_{2}}Y_{2}^{\prime},\cdots,\tau^{*}_{E}\sqrt{\rho_{E}}Z_{E}+\tau_{E}^{*}\sqrt{1-\rho_{E}}Y_{E}^{\prime}), $$

and $\{Z_{e}\}$ , $\{Y_{e}\}$ , $\{Y_{e}^{\prime}\}$ are a total of $(3E)$ iid $\mathcal{N}(0,I_{p})$ variables. Then $H_{e}$ can be further rewritten with a function $\nu:\mathbb{R}^{p}\to\mathbb{R}^{p}$ as follows:

$$ \displaystyle H_{e}= \displaystyle\frac{\mathbb{E}[W_{e}^{2}]}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}}+\frac{\kappa_{e}}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}}\cdot\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbb{E}\left[\nu(\sqrt{\rho_{1}}Z_{1}+\sqrt{1-\rho_{1}}Y_{1})^{{\top}}\nu(\sqrt{\rho_{1}}Z_{1}+\sqrt{1-\rho_{1}}Y_{1}^{\prime})\middle|Z_{2},Z_{3},\cdots,Z_{E}\right]\right], \displaystyle\nu(\cdot)= \displaystyle\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\left\{\mathbb{E}\left[\eta(\tau_{1}^{*}(\,\cdot\,),\tau^{*}_{2}\sqrt{\rho_{2}}Z_{2}+\tau_{2}^{*}\sqrt{1-\rho_{2}}Y_{2},\cdots,\tau^{*}_{E}\sqrt{\rho_{E}}Z_{E}+\tau_{E}^{*}\sqrt{1-\rho_{E}}Y_{E})\middle|Z_{2},Z_{3},\cdots,Z_{E}\right]\right\}. $$

We introduce a total of $p$ iid stationary Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes with covariance function $\exp\left(-t\right)$ , stacked as a vector $X_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{p}$ , then $H_{e}^{(p)}=\frac{\mathbb{E}[W_{e}^{2}]}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}}+\frac{\kappa_{e}}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}}\cdot\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbb{E}\left[\nu(X_{0})^{{\top}}\nu(X_{t})\middle|Z_{2},Z_{3},\cdots,Z_{E}\right]\right]$ , $t=\log(1/\rho_{1})$ . With the same eigen-decomposition trick as that of Lemma C.1 of Bayati and Montanari [32], or Lemma C.2 of Donoho and Montanari [33], we can show $H_{e}^{{(p)}}$ is increasing and strictly convex in $\rho_{1}\in[0,1]$ , and thus so is $H_{e}$ . We have proved the first half of Proposition C.7.

To show $0\leq\frac{\partial H_{e}}{\partial\rho_{i}}\leq\frac{\kappa_{e}(\tau_{i}^{*})^{2}\varpi_{i}^{*}}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}\varpi^{*}_{e}}\overline{\delta}_{i}\overline{\delta}_{e}$ , we only need to show $0\leq\frac{\partial H_{e}}{\partial\rho_{i}}(\vec{1}_{E})\leq\frac{\kappa_{e}(\tau_{i}^{*})^{2}\varpi_{i}^{*}}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}\varpi^{*}_{e}}\overline{\delta}_{i}\overline{\delta}_{e}$ , where $\vec{1}_{E}$ is a vector of all ones in $R^{E}$ . $$ \displaystyle\frac{\partial H_{e}}{\partial\rho_{1}}= \displaystyle\frac{\kappa_{e}\tau_{1}^{*}}{(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}}\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[(\overline{\eta}_{(2)}-\beta_{e})^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}J_{1}(\overline{\eta}_{(1)})\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\rho_{1}}}Z_{1}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-\rho_{1}}}Y_{1}\right)\right], $$

It is already known that $S^{t}(c)=\{j\in[p]:\lvert\tilde{\eta}^{t}_{j}\rvert\geq\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\vec{\lambda}_{j}(1-c)\}$ , $\widetilde{S}(c)=\{j\in[p]:\lvert\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}^{t}_{j}\rvert\geq\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\vec{\lambda}_{j}(1-c)\}$ . By Lemma C.2, for any already chosen and fixed $a$ , as $p\to\infty$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\left\lvert{\lvert S^{t}(c)\rvert}/{p}-\mathbb{E}[{\lvert\overline{S}(c)\rvert}/{p}]\right\rvert\leq \displaystyle\lvert\phi_{1}^{(p)}(\tilde{\eta}^{t})-\mathbb{E}[\phi_{1}^{(p)}(\overline{\widetilde{\eta}})]\rvert+\phi_{2}^{(p)}(\tilde{\eta}^{t})+\mathbb{E}[\phi_{2}^{(p)}(\overline{\widetilde{\eta}})]\leq 2\mathbb{E}[\phi_{2}^{(p)}(\overline{\widetilde{\eta}})]+o_{\mathsf{P}}(1) \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{2}{p}\sum_{j\in[p]}\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{1}{\{\lvert\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}_{j}\rvert\in(\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c)-2a,\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c)+a)\}}]+o_{\mathsf{P}}(1). $$

By Lemma C.8, for any $\epsilon>0$ , we can fix a small $a$ s.t. $\sup_{p}\frac{1}{p}\sum_{j\in[p]}\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{1}{\{\lvert\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}_{j}\rvert\in(\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c)-2a,\widetilde{\theta}^{*}(1-c)+a)\}}]<\epsilon/4$ before taking $p\to\infty$ . Thus Lemma C.9 is proved. ∎

#### Proof of Lemma C.5.

For any chosen and fixed $c\in(0,1)$ , we know from Lemma C.9, $\lvert S^{t}(c)\rvert/p=\mathbb{E}[\lvert\overline{S}(c)\rvert/p]+o_{\mathsf{P}}(1)$ as $p\to\infty$ . Furthermore,

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\lvert\overline{S}(c)\rvert/p]= \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\sum_{j\in[p]}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbf{1}{\{\lvert\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}_{j}\rvert>\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\vec{\lambda}_{j}\}}\right]+\frac{1}{p}\sum_{j\in[p]}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbf{1}{\{\lvert\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}_{j}\rvert\in(\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\vec{\lambda}_{j}(1-c),\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\vec{\lambda}_{j}]\}}\right]. $$

Lemma C.8 implies $\forall\,\epsilon>0$ , $\exists\,c\in(0,1)$ small enough s.t. $\sup_{p}\frac{1}{p}\sum_{j\in[p]}\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{1}{\{\lvert\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}_{j}\rvert\in(\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\vec{\lambda}_{j}(1-c),\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\vec{\lambda}_{j})\}}]<\epsilon$ . By the definition of $\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\sum_{j\in[p]}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbf{1}{\{\lvert\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}_{j}\rvert>\widetilde{\theta}^{*}\vec{\lambda}_{j}\}}\right]= \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\lVert\overline{\eta}\rVert_{0}\right]=\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}^{(p)}\to\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}, $$

where the second equality is by Equation (B-6) and the convergence is by Proposition 1.

By the choice of $c$ so far, we know it only depends on the ‘idealized’ quantities such as $\overline{\eta}$ and $\overline{\widetilde{\eta}}$ , not any specific time step $t$ . As a result, $\forall\,\epsilon>0$ , there exists $c=c(\epsilon)\in(0,1)$ s.t. fixing any $c^{\prime}\in(0,c]$ and any $t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ , we have $\lim_{p}\mathbb{P}\left[\lvert S^{t}(c^{\prime})\rvert/p\leq\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}+\epsilon\right]=1$ . This completes the proof. ∎

#### C.1.6 Proof of Lemma C.6

We need to introduce Lemma C.10 as preparation for the proof of Lemma C.6.

First off, we assume without loss of generality that $\pi_{e}>0$ for all $e\in[E]$ ; that is, all the environments $(y_{e},{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2})$ that have contributed to $\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}$ have been assigned positive weights in the loss function in Equation (2). This does not lose generality because by Assumption 2 and 4(a), $\pi_{e}=0$ iff $\varpi_{e}^{*}=0$ ; in other words, when one environment is assigned no weight in the loss function in Equation (2), it does not enter the GLAMP formulation either, so we can just ignore it.

Secondly, let $N=\sum_{e\in[E]}n_{e}$ , $\kappa=\lim_{p}p/N=(\sum_{e\in[E]}\kappa_{E}^{-1})^{-1}$ , and define

$$ y_{\mathrm{stack}}=\begin{bmatrix}\sqrt{\pi_{1}}y_{1}\\
\sqrt{\pi_{2}}y_{2}\\
\vdots\\
\sqrt{\pi_{E}}y_{E}\end{bmatrix},X_{\mathrm{stack}}=\begin{bmatrix}\sqrt{\pi_{1}}{X_{1}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\\
\sqrt{\pi_{2}}{X_{2}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{2}^{1/2}\\
\vdots\\
\sqrt{\pi_{E}}{X_{E}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{E}^{1/2}\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\sqrt{\frac{n_{1}}{N}}{X_{1}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{\pi_{1}N}{n_{1}}}\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\\
\sqrt{\frac{n_{2}}{N}}{X_{2}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{\pi_{2}N}{n_{2}}}\Sigma_{2}^{1/2}\\
\vdots\\
\sqrt{\frac{n_{E}}{N}}{X_{E}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{\pi_{E}N}{n_{E}}}\Sigma_{E}^{1/2}.\end{bmatrix} $$

Now we can rewrite the loss function in Equation (2) as $L(b)=\frac{1}{2}\lVert y_{\mathrm{stack}}-X_{\mathrm{stack}}b\rVert_{2}^{2}+\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda})b\rVert_{1}$ .

Lastly, define the sparse singular eigenvalues of a matrix. For any matrix $X$ having $p$ columns, any subset $S\subset[p]$ , define $\kappa_{-}(X,S)=\inf\left\{\lVert Xu\rVert_{2}:\mathrm{supp}(u)\subset S,\lVert u\rVert_{2}=1\right\}$ and the $k$ -sparse singular value

$$ \kappa_{-}(X,k)=\min_{S\subset[p],\lvert S\rvert\leq k}\kappa_{-}(X,S). $$

Of course $\kappa_{-}(X,k)$ is decreasing in $k$ for fixed $X$ ; when $k\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$ , the definition in Equation (C-22) can be equivalently written as $\kappa_{-}(X,k)=\min_{S\subset[p],\lvert S\rvert=k}\kappa_{-}(X,S)$ .

#### Lemma C.10 (Lower Bound on the Sparse Singular Values).

Under Assumption 2 and the definition in Equation (C-21), there exists small enough constants $\epsilon_{0}>0$ and $c_{0}>0$ , s.t. $\kappa\cdot(\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}+\epsilon_{0})<1$ , and $\forall\,\epsilon\in(0,\epsilon_{0})$ ,

$$ \lim_{p\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\left[\kappa_{-}\left(X_{\mathrm{stack}},p(\textstyle\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}+\epsilon)\right)>c_{0}\right]=1. $$

#### Proof of Lemma C.10.

We use $X_{\mathrm{temp}}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times p}$ to denote a matrix of iid $\mathcal{N}(0,1/N)$ elements, and divide it into blocks as $(X_{\mathrm{temp}})^{{\top}}=\left[(X_{\mathrm{temp},1})^{{\top}}|(X_{\mathrm{temp},2})^{{\top}}|\cdots|(X_{\mathrm{temp},E})^{{\top}}\right]$ , where $X_{\mathrm{temp},e}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{e}\times p}$ . For $X_{\mathrm{stack}}$ in Equation (C-21), and any index set $S\subset[p]$ , the following equality in distribution holds:

$$ (X_{\mathrm{stack}})_{\cdot,S}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{d}}}{{=}}\begin{bmatrix}(X_{\mathrm{temp},1})_{\cdot,S}\left({\frac{\pi_{1}N}{n_{1}}}(\Sigma_{1})_{S,S}\right)^{1/2}\\
(X_{\mathrm{temp},2})_{\cdot,S}\left({\frac{\pi_{2}N}{n_{2}}}(\Sigma_{2})_{S,S}\right)^{1/2}\\
\vdots\\
(X_{\mathrm{temp},E})_{\cdot,S}\left({\frac{\pi_{E}N}{n_{E}}}(\Sigma_{E})_{S,S}\right)^{1/2}.\end{bmatrix} $$

To see why the equality in distribution holds, note that each block of $(X_{\mathrm{stack}})_{\cdot,S}$ satisfies $[\sqrt{\frac{n_{e}}{N}}{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{\pi_{e}N}{n_{e}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}]_{\cdot,S}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{d}}}{{=}}[X_{\mathrm{temp},e}(\sqrt{\frac{\pi_{e}N}{n_{e}}}\Sigma_{e})^{1/2}]_{\cdot,S}=X_{\mathrm{temp},e}[(\sqrt{\frac{\pi_{e}N}{n_{e}}}\Sigma_{e})^{1/2}]_{\cdot,S}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times\lvert S\rvert}$ . Each row of $X_{\mathrm{temp},e}[(\sqrt{\frac{\pi_{e}N}{n_{e}}}\Sigma_{e})^{1/2}]_{\cdot,S}$ is an iid draw from $\mathcal{N}(0,\frac{\pi_{e}N}{n_{e}}(\Sigma_{e})_{S,S})$ , so the block is equal in distribution to $(X_{\mathrm{temp},e})_{\cdot,S}({\frac{\pi_{e}N}{n_{e}}}(\Sigma_{e})_{S,S})^{1/2}$ .

Since $\liminf_{p\to\infty}\min_{e\in[E]}\{\lambda_{\min}(\frac{\pi_{e}N}{n_{e}}\Sigma_{e})\}\geq\min_{e}\{\pi_{e}\kappa_{e}\}/(c_{1}\kappa)$ , there exists some non-random large enough $p_{0}$ s.t. $\forall\,p\geq p_{0}$ , $\min_{S\subset[p],e\in[E]}\{\lambda_{\min}(\frac{\pi_{e}N}{n_{e}}(\Sigma_{e})_{S,S})\}\geq\min_{e}\{\pi_{e}\kappa_{e}\}/(2c_{1}\kappa)$ . For $p\geq p_{0}$ , we can invoke Lemma F.6 to get $\mathbb{P}[\sigma_{\min}\left((X_{\mathrm{stack}})_{\cdot,S}\right)\leq c]\leq\mathbb{P}[(\min_{e}\{\pi_{e}\kappa_{e}\}/(2c_{1}\kappa))^{1/2}\sigma_{\min}((X_{\mathrm{temp}})_{\cdot,S})\leq c],\ \forall\,c>0$ . When we think about all the possible index sets $S\subset[p],\lvert S\rvert=k\leq p$ for some $k\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$ ,

$$ \mathbb{P}\left[\kappa_{-}(X_{\mathrm{stack}},k)\leq c\right]\leq\binom{p}{k}\mathbb{P}\left[\sigma_{\min}((X_{\mathrm{temp}})_{\cdot,S})\leq\frac{c}{(\min_{e}\{\pi_{e}\kappa_{e}\}/(2c_{1}\kappa))^{1/2}}\right],\ \forall\,c>0, $$

where we have used a union bound over all possible $S\subset[p],\lvert S\rvert=k$ and the fact that $(X_{\mathrm{temp}})_{\cdot,S}$ has the same marginal distribution for any $S\subset[p],\lvert S\rvert=k$ .

Everything from here follows exactly the same steps as those of Lemma 5, Huang [81] (specifically, after its Equation (63)). With the same proof, we arrive at the following fact: For $k\in\mathbb{N}_{+}$ , if $\lim_{N}\frac{k}{N}=\omega\in(0,+\infty)$ , and additionally $\omega\in(0,1)$ only when $\kappa\geq 1$ , then there exists some small constant $c^{\prime}$ and large $p_{0}$ s.t. fixing any small $c\in(0,c^{\prime})$ , the non-asymptotic bound holds $\forall\,p\geq p_{0}$ :

$$ \mathbb{P}\left[\kappa_{-}(X_{\mathrm{stack}},k)\leq c\right]\leq C_{1}\exp\left(-C_{2}\cdot p\right)\quad\text{for some constants }C_{1},C_{2}>0. $$

We argue $\lfloor p(\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}+\epsilon)\rfloor$ qualifies as the choice of ‘ $k$ ’ in the above fact for small enough $\epsilon>0$ . $\lim_{p}p(\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}+\epsilon)/N=\kappa\,(\sum_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}+\epsilon)$ . Assumption 4(a) implies $\overline{\delta}_{e}<\kappa_{e}^{-1}$ , so $\kappa\sum_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}<1$ . We can make $\epsilon$ small enough s.t. $\kappa(\sum_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}+\epsilon)$ is strictly smaller than one when it is needed for $\kappa\geq 1$ . The proof is then complete after taking $p\to\infty$ . ∎

We are finally ready to prove Lemma C.6.

#### Proof of Lemma C.6.

We still assume without loss of generality that $\pi_{e}>0$ for all $e\in[E]$ . Recall the loss function defined in Equation (2) and re-expressed as $L(b)=\frac{1}{2}\lVert y_{\mathrm{stack}}-X_{\mathrm{stack}}\beta\rVert_{2}^{2}+\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda})b\rVert_{1}$ . Define $\Delta\eta^{t}=\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}-\eta^{t}$ . Since $\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}$ minimizes the loss, $L(\eta^{t}+\Delta\eta^{t})\leq L(\eta^{t})$ .

Applying Lemma F.6(b) and then Lemma F.4(a) to $X_{\mathrm{stack}}$ defined in Equation (C-21), we know $\sigma_{\max}(X_{\mathrm{stack}})\leq 2(\max_{e}\{\pi_{e}\kappa_{e}\}c_{1}/\kappa)^{1/2}(1+\sqrt{\kappa})$ holds almost surely as $p\to\infty$ .

We now define the high-probability event we will be working on throughout the proof. We choose $\epsilon_{0}\in(0,1)$ small enough and $M>1$ large enough s.t. $\forall\,\epsilon\in(0,\epsilon_{0})$ , $\exists\,T$ s.t. $\forall\,t\geq T$ , at the time step $t$ , the following conditions are satisfied simultaneously with probability going to 1 as $p\to\infty$ :

- (i) $\max\{\frac{1}{\sqrt{p}}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2},\frac{1}{\sqrt{p}}\lVert\eta^{t}\rVert_{2},\frac{1}{\sqrt{p}}\lVert\vec{\lambda}\rVert_{2}\}\leq M$ (by Lemma C.1, Lemma C.2 and Assumption 3(a));

- (ii) $\lvert S^{t}(c_{2})\rvert\leq p(\sum_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}+{\epsilon})$ for some $c_{2}=c_{2}(\epsilon)\in(0,1)$ (by Lemma C.5 with $c_{2}$ depending on the specific $\epsilon\in(0,\epsilon_{0})$ but invariant to the choice of the time step $t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ );

- (iii) $\kappa_{-}(X_{\mathrm{stack}},p(\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}+2{\epsilon}))>c_{3}$ for some $c_{3}=c_{3}(\epsilon_{0})\in(0,1)$ (by Lemma C.10 with $c_{3}$ depending on the upper bound $\epsilon_{0}$ );

- (iv) $\frac{1}{\sqrt{p}}\lVert\nabla L(\eta^{t})\rVert_{2}<\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}/(2M^{2})$ (by Lemma C.4; the only condition that determines the choice of $T$ );

- (v) $\sigma_{\max}(X_{\mathrm{stack}})\leq c_{4}=2(\max_{e}\{\pi_{e}\kappa_{e}\}c_{1}/\kappa)^{1/2}(1+\sqrt{\kappa})$ .

In particular, the use of Lemma C.10 in condition (iii) has also required $\kappa\,(\sum_{e\in[E]}\overline{\delta}_{e}+2{\epsilon_{0}})<1$ which will be needed later. We also let $c_{5}>0$ be a value that satisfies $\liminf_{p}\min_{j\in[p]}\{\vec{\lambda}_{j}\}>c_{5}$ by Assumption 3(a).

Let $S=\mathrm{supp}(\eta^{t})\subset[p]$ . Recall $s^{t}$ defined in Equation (C-14) from Lemma C.4 is a sub-gradient of $\lVert\eta^{t}\rVert_{1}$ , and $\nabla L(\eta^{t})$ in Lemma C.4 is defined using $s^{t}$ . We have the following inequalities:

$$ \displaystyle 0\geq \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\left[L(\eta^{t}+\Delta\eta^{t})-L(\eta^{t})\right] \displaystyle\geq \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\left(\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S})(\eta^{t}_{S}+\Delta\eta^{t}_{S})\rVert_{1}-\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S})\eta^{t}_{S}\rVert_{1}\right)+\frac{1}{p}\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}})\Delta\eta^{t}_{S^{c}}\rVert_{1}+\frac{1}{2p}\lVert X_{\mathrm{stack}}\Delta\eta^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2} \displaystyle-\frac{1}{p}(y_{\mathrm{stack}}-X_{\mathrm{stack}}\eta^{t})^{{\top}}X_{\mathrm{stack}}\Delta\eta^{t} \displaystyle\geq \displaystyle\underbrace{\frac{1}{p}\left(\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S})(\eta^{t}_{S}+\Delta\eta^{t}_{S})\rVert_{1}-\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S})\eta^{t}_{S}\rVert_{1}-\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S})\mathop{\mathrm{sign}}(\eta^{t}_{S})^{{\top}}\Delta\eta^{t}_{S}\right)}_{(1)} \displaystyle+\underbrace{\frac{1}{p}\left(\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}})\Delta\eta^{t}_{S^{c}}\rVert_{1}-[\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}})s^{t}_{S^{c}}]^{{}^{{\top}}}\Delta\eta^{t}_{S^{c}}\right)}_{(2)}+\underbrace{\frac{1}{2p}\lVert X_{\mathrm{stack}}\Delta\eta^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2}}_{(3)} \displaystyle+\frac{1}{p}(\nabla L(\eta^{t}))^{{\top}}\Delta\eta^{t}. $$

The terms $(1)$ , $(2)$ and $(3)$ are all non-negative. In particular for $(1)$ , we can use the following inequality for any two real numbers $a,b$ : $\lvert a+b\rvert\geq\lvert a\rvert+b\cdot\mathop{\mathrm{sign}}(a)$ . Since the terms $(1)$ , $(2)$ and $(3)$ are all non-negative, we must have $(\nabla L(\eta^{t}))^{{\top}}\Delta\eta^{t}\leq 0$ . By conditions (i), (iv) of the high-probability event and Cauchy’s inequality, we know

$$ \lim_{p\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\left[(1)+(2)+(3)\leq\frac{1}{p}\lvert(\nabla L(\eta^{t}))^{{\top}}\Delta\eta^{t}\rvert\leq\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}/M\right]=1. $$

Respectively for terms (2) and (3), the above tells us on the high probability event,

$$ \displaystyle 0\leq \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}})\Delta\eta^{t}_{S^{c}}\rVert_{1}-\frac{1}{p}[\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}})s^{t}_{S^{c}}]^{{\top}}\Delta\eta^{t}_{S^{c}}\leq\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}/M, \displaystyle 0\leq \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\lVert X_{\mathrm{stack}}\Delta\eta^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq 2\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}/M. $$

Take the SVD of $X_{\mathrm{stack}}:\,X_{\mathrm{stack}}=\sum_{i=1}^{N\land p}\sigma_{i}u_{i}v_{i}^{{\top}}$ , assuming $\sigma_{1}\geq\sigma_{2}\geq\cdots\geq\sigma_{N\land p}$ . Let $V_{(1)}=\Span(v_{i}:\sigma_{i}\geq c_{3}/2)$ and $V_{(2)}$ be the orthogonal complement of $V_{(1)}$ in $\mathbb{R}^{p}$ . Let $P_{(1)},P_{(2)}$ be the projection matrices of $V_{(1)}$ and $V_{(2)}$ . Denote $X_{(1)}=X_{\mathrm{stack}}P_{(1)}$ and $X_{(1)}=X_{\mathrm{stack}}P_{(2)}$ . Then $X_{(1)}^{{\top}}X_{(2)}=0$ . Define $\Delta\eta_{(1)}=P_{(1)}\Delta\eta^{t}$ , $\Delta\eta_{(2)}=P_{(2)}\Delta\eta^{t}$ . The second line of Equation (C-23) implies

$$ \frac{1}{p}\lVert X_{(1)}\Delta\eta_{(1)}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq 2\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}/M,\quad\frac{1}{p}\lVert X_{(2)}\Delta\eta_{(2)}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq 2\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}/M. $$

For $\Delta\eta_{(1)}$ corresponding to the larger singular values, we consequently have

$$ \frac{1}{p}\lVert\Delta\eta_{(1)}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq 8\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}/(c_{3}^{2})\leq 8\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{2}/M, $$

and we are left to bound $\frac{1}{p}\lVert\Delta\eta_{(2)}\rVert_{2}^{2}$ .

We use the first line of Equation (C-23) to bound $\frac{1}{p}\lVert\Delta\eta_{(2)}\rVert_{2}^{2}$ . For $\Delta\eta_{(1)}$ , we have

$$ \frac{1}{p}[\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}})s^{t}_{S^{c}}]^{{\top}}(\Delta\eta_{(1)})_{S^{c}}\leq\frac{1}{p}\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}})(\Delta\eta_{(1)})_{S^{c}}\rVert_{1}\leq\frac{1}{\sqrt{p}}\lVert\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}}\rVert\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt{p}}\lVert\Delta\hat{\beta}_{(1)}\rVert_{2}\leq 2\sqrt{2}\epsilon c_{2}c_{3}, $$

where we have used Cauchy’s inequality and the bound on $\frac{1}{\sqrt{p}}\lVert\vec{\lambda}\rVert_{2}$ from (i) of the high-probability event. Since $\Delta\eta_{(2)}=\Delta\eta^{t}-\Delta\eta_{(1)}$ , we know

$$ \frac{1}{p}\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}})(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{c}}\rVert_{1}-\frac{1}{p}[\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{c}})s^{t}_{S^{c}}]^{{\top}}(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{c}}\leq\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}+4\sqrt{2}\epsilon c_{2}c_{3}, $$

where we have used the fact that $M>1$ from (i). Recall that for $S^{t}(c_{2})$ defined in Lemma C.5, $S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}\subset S^{c}$ . Hence,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\lVert\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}})(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}}\rVert_{1}-\frac{1}{p}[\diag(\vec{\lambda}_{S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}})s^{t}_{S^{c}}]^{{\top}}(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}}\leq \displaystyle\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}+4\sqrt{2}\epsilon c_{2}c_{3} \displaystyle\iff\frac{1}{p}\sum_{j\in S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}}\vec{\lambda}_{j}\left[\left\lvert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{j}\right\rvert-s^{t}_{j}(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{j}\right]\leq \displaystyle\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}+4\sqrt{2}\epsilon c_{2}c_{3}. $$

By the definition of $S^{t}(c_{2})$ , $\forall\,j\in S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}$ , $\lvert s^{t}_{j}\rvert<1-c_{2}$ . Also recall we have defined $c_{5}$ to be a constant s.t. $\liminf_{p}\min_{j\in[p]}\{\vec{\lambda}_{j}\}>c_{5}$ . As a result,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}}\rVert_{1}\leq\frac{1}{c_{2}c_{5}}\left(\epsilon^{2}\cdot c_{2}^{2}c_{3}^{4}/M+4\sqrt{2}\epsilon c_{2}c_{3}\right)\leq(1+4\sqrt{2})\epsilon c_{3}/c_{5}. $$

Recall we have chosen $\kappa\,(\sum_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}+2{\epsilon})<1$ as required by Lemma C.10 used for condition (iii) of the high-probability event. Condition (ii) guarantees $\lvert S^{t}(c_{2})\rvert\leq p(\sum_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}+{\epsilon})$ . Then we immediately know $\lvert S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}\rvert>p{\epsilon}$ , because otherwise $p=\lvert S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}\rvert+\lvert S^{t}(c_{2})\rvert\leq p(\sum_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}+2{\epsilon})<p$ would give a contradiction. We partition $S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}$ disjointly into $S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}=\cup_{l=1}^{K}S_{l}$ , with each $S_{l}$ satisfying $\lvert S_{l}\rvert\in[p{\epsilon}/2,p{\epsilon}]$ , and they are constructed in a descending order in the sense that for any $i\in S_{l}$ and $j\in S_{l+1}$ , $\lvert({\Delta}\eta_{(2)})_{i}\rvert\geq\lvert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{j}\rvert$ . By the disjoint partition,

$$ \frac{1}{p}\lVert\Delta\eta_{(2)}\rVert_{2}^{2}=\frac{1}{p}\left\lVert\left(\Delta\eta_{(2)}\right)_{\cup_{l=2}^{K}S_{l}}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}+\frac{1}{p}\left\lVert\left(\Delta\eta_{(2)}\right)_{S^{t}(c_{2})\cup S_{1}}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}. $$

We bound the two terms on the RHS respectively. For the first term,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\left\lVert\left(\Delta\eta_{(2)}\right)_{\cup_{l=2}^{K}S_{l}}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}= \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\sum_{l=2}^{K}\left\lVert\left(\Delta\eta_{(2)}\right)_{S_{l}}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq\frac{1}{p}\sum_{l=2}^{K}\lvert S_{l}\rvert\cdot\left(\frac{\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S_{l-1}}\rVert_{1}}{\lvert S_{l-1}\rvert}\right)^{2} \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\cdot\frac{4}{p\epsilon}\sum_{l=2}^{K}\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S_{l-1}}\rVert_{1}^{2}\leq\frac{1}{p}\cdot\frac{4}{p{\epsilon}}\left[\sum_{l=2}^{K}\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S_{l-1}}\rVert_{1}\right]^{2} \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{4}{p^{2}{\epsilon}}\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{t}(c_{2})^{c}}\rVert_{1}^{2}\leq 4\epsilon c_{3}^{2}(1+4\sqrt{2})^{2}/c_{5}^{2}, $$

where the first inequality is because $\forall\,i\in S_{l}$ , $\lvert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{i}\rvert^{2}\leq({\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S_{l-1}}\rVert_{1}}/{\lvert S_{l-1}\rvert})^{2}$ ; the second inequality is because $\lvert S_{l}\rvert\in[p{\epsilon}/2,p{\epsilon}]$ for all $l\in[K]$ ; the last inequality is by Equation (C-25).

For the second term, we apply conditions (iii), (v) of the high-probability event:

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{t}(c_{2})\cup S_{1}}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq \displaystyle\frac{1}{pc_{3}^{2}}\left\lVert(X_{\mathrm{stack}})_{\cdot,S^{t}(c_{2})\cup S_{1}}(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{t}(c_{2})\cup S_{1}}\right\rVert_{2}^{2} \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{2}{pc_{3}^{2}}\left[\left\lVert X_{\mathrm{stack}}\Delta\eta_{(2)}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}+\left\lVert(X_{\mathrm{stack}})_{\cdot,\cup_{l=2}^{K}S_{l}}(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{{}_{\cup_{l=2}^{K}S_{l}}}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right] \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{2}{pc_{3}^{2}}\left[\frac{c_{3}^{2}}{4}\left(\left\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{t}(c_{2})\cup S_{1}}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}+\left\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{\cup_{l=2}^{K}S_{l}}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right)+c_{4}^{2}\,\left\lVert\left(\Delta\eta_{(2)}\right)_{\cup_{l=2}^{K}S_{l}}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{1}{2p}\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{S^{t}(c_{2})\cup S_{1}}\rVert_{2}^{2}+\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{2c_{4}^{2}}{c_{3}^{2}}\right)\frac{1}{p}\lVert(\Delta\eta_{(2)})_{\cup_{l=2}^{K}S_{l}}\rVert_{2}^{2}, $$

where the first inequality has used condition (iii); the second inequality is by the triangle inequality; the terms involving ‘ $c_{3}$ ’ after the third inequality is because $\Delta\eta_{(2)}$ is $\Delta\eta^{t}$ projected onto $V_{(2)}$ corresponding to the smaller or null singular values of $X_{\mathrm{stack}}$ . #### Definition D.2 (State Evolution).

### D.1 Proof of Lemma D.1

#### Proof of Lemma D.1.

Just like the proof of Lemma C.2, we specify a multi-environment GLAMP instance that has the form and state evolution as described in Definitions D.1 and D.2. Also analogously to the proof of Lemma C.2, we can use a sub-sequence based argument to address the technicality caused by using random initialization in the GLAMP instance. We then move on to describe the instance itself.

Same as the GLAMP instance for the stack Lasso estimator, let $\{q_{e}:e\in[E]\}$ all be sufficiently large and fixed integers, let $B=[\beta_{1}|\beta_{2}|\cdots|\beta_{E}|\eta^{0}|0|0|\cdots]\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}$ , and $W_{e}=[w_{e}|0|0|\cdots]\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{e}\times q}$ . We add ‘ind’ to the subscripts to differentiate from the iterates for the stacked Lasso; starting from $V_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{0}=0$ and $R_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{0}=[{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\beta_{e}|{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\eta_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{0}|0|\cdots]$ , we specify the GLAMP instance as follows: ( $t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ )

$$ \displaystyle\forall\,e\in[E],\ V_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t}= \displaystyle\left[v_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{1}|v_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{2}|\cdots|v_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t}|0|0|\cdots\right], \displaystyle\eta_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t}(V_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t})= \displaystyle\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\left[\beta_{e}|\eta_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{0}|\eta_{e}(v_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{1})|\eta_{e}(v_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{2})|\cdots|\eta_{e}(v_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t})|0|0|\cdots\right], \displaystyle R_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t}= \displaystyle[{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\beta_{e}|r_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{0}|r_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{1}|\cdots|r_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t}|0|0|\cdots], \displaystyle\Psi_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t}(R_{e}^{t})= \displaystyle\kappa_{e}[y_{e}-r_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{0}|y_{e}-r_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{1}|\cdots|y_{e}-r_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t}|0|0|\cdots]\quad(y_{e}={X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\beta_{e}+w_{e}). $$

Now we know the GLAMP iterates take the form

$$ \displaystyle v_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t}= \displaystyle{\displaystyle X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}}(y_{e}-r_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t-1})-\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\beta_{e}+\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\eta_{e}(v_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t-1}), \displaystyle r_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t}= \displaystyle{\displaystyle X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\eta_{e}(v_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t})-\kappa_{e}(y_{e}-r_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t-1})\cdot\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\left(\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\frac{\partial\eta_{E}}{\partial v_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{t}}(Z_{e}^{t})\right)\right], $$

where the Gaussian variables used are characterized by the state evolution which we are yet to study.

To fully write out the form of the GLAMP iterates, we need to find the state evolution first. We discard the all-zero columns in $V_{e}^{t}$ and $R_{e}^{t}$ , start from $\Sigma_{(\mathrm{ind},R,e)}^{0}$ and compute the first two covariance matrices for the state evolution. From there, we prove the whole state evolution for $V^{t}_{e}$ with induction.

- 1. $\Sigma_{(\mathrm{ind},R,e)}^{0}=\begin{bmatrix}\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\beta_{e}&\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}_{e}]\\ \lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}_{e}]&\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\overline{\eta}_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}_{e}]\\ \end{bmatrix}$ .

- 2. $\Sigma_{(\mathrm{ind},V,e)}^{1}=\lim_{p}\frac{1}{n_{e}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert w_{e}+(Z_{(\mathrm{ind},R,e)}^{0})_{1}-(Z_{(\mathrm{ind},R,e)}^{0})_{2}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right]$ where $Z^{0}_{(\mathrm{ind},R,e)}=[(Z_{(\mathrm{ind},R,e)}^{0})_{1}|(Z_{(\mathrm{ind},R,e)}^{0})_{2}]\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times 2}$ has iid rows drawn from $\mathcal{N}(0,\kappa_{e}\Sigma_{(\mathrm{ind},R,e)}^{0})$ . Simplifying it with Assumption 5 and 6, $\Sigma_{(\mathrm{ind},V,e)}^{1}=\mathbb{E}[W_{e}^{2}]+\kappa_{e}\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\lVert\overline{\eta}_{e}-\beta_{e}\rVert_{\Sigma_{(\mathrm{ind},e)}}^{2}]=(\tau_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{*})^{2}$ .

- 3. $\Sigma_{(\mathrm{ind},R,e)}^{1}=\begin{bmatrix}\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\beta_{e}&\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}_{e}]&\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}_{e}]\\ \lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}_{e}]&\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\overline{\eta}_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}_{e}]&\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\overline{\eta}_{e,(1)}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}_{e,(2)}\right]\\ \lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\beta_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}]&\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\overline{\eta}_{e,(1)}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}_{e,(2)}\right]&\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}[\overline{\eta}_{e}^{{\top}}\Sigma_{e}\overline{\eta}_{e}],\end{bmatrix}$ where $\overline{\eta}_{e,(1)}$ and $\overline{\eta}_{e,(2)}$ are mutually independent copies of $\overline{\eta}_{e}$ .

For the diagonal term, $(\Sigma_{(\mathrm{ind},V,e)}^{t+1})_{t+1,t+1}=\lim_{p}\frac{1}{n_{e}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert w_{e}+(Z_{(\mathrm{ind},R,e)}^{0})_{1}-(Z_{(\mathrm{ind},R,e)}^{t})_{t+2}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right]=(\tau_{\mathrm{ind},e}^{*})^{2}$ using the same simplification as that of $\Sigma_{(\mathrm{ind},V,e)}^{1}$ .

where $\overline{\eta}_{e,(1)}$ and $\overline{\eta}_{e,(2)}$ are mutually independent copies of $\overline{\eta}_{e}$ .

Now we have verified the GLAMP iterates take the form of Definition D.1 and their state evolution is described by Definition D.2. By GLAMP convergence, we have shown Lemma D.1. ∎

### E.1 Proof of Auxiliary Lemmas in Section E

#### E.1.1 Proof of Lemma E.1

The proof follows the exact same steps as those of our Lemma C.1, or Lemma 3.2 of Bayati and Montanari [32], so we only point out some key steps this time. By Assumption 2 and Lemma C.1, we know there exists $M_{1}>0$ s.t. $\limsup_{p}L_{\textup{II}}(\hat{\beta}_{\textup{II}})/p\leq\limsup_{p}L_{\textup{II}}(0)/p\leq M_{1}$ .

If $\kappa_{1}<1$ , then we have $\liminf_{p}\sigma_{\min}({X_{1}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{1}^{1/2})\geq(1-\sqrt{\kappa_{1}})/c_{1}^{1/2}>0$ using Lemma F.4 and Assumption 2. In this case, we would have proved Lemma E.1. For the rest of the proof, we focus on the case of $\kappa_{1}\geq 1$ .

Let $P_{1}^{\|}$ be the projection matrix onto $\mathrm{\ker}({X_{1}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{1}^{1/2})$ and $P_{1}^{\bot}$ onto $\mathrm{\ker}({X_{1}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{1}^{1/2})^{\bot}$ . Following the same argument as that of Lemma C.1 and Lemma 3.2 of Bayati and Montanari [32], we know from Kashin’s theorem that there exists some constant $B_{1}$ , s.t. almost surely as $p\to\infty$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{p}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\textup{II}}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq B_{1}\left(\frac{1}{p}\lVert P_{1}^{\|}\hat{\beta}_{\textup{II}}\rVert_{1}\right)^{2}+\frac{1}{p}\lVert P_{1}^{\bot}\hat{\beta}_{\textup{II}}\rVert_{2}^{2}\leq 2B_{1}\left(\frac{1}{p}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\textup{II}}\rVert_{1}\right)^{2}+\frac{2B_{1}+1}{p}\lVert P_{1}^{\bot}\hat{\beta}_{\textup{II}}\rVert_{2}^{2}, $$

where $\frac{1}{p}\lVert\hat{\beta}_{\textup{II}}\rVert_{1}$ is bounded by some non-random constant $M_{2}$ almost surely since $\frac{1}{p}L_{\textup{II}}(\hat{\beta}_{\textup{II}})$ is bounded.

Because $\mathrm{\ker}({X_{1}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{1}^{1/2})^{\bot}=\mathrm{range}(\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}{X_{1}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}})$ , $P_{1}^{\bot}=\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}{X_{1}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}}({X_{1}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{1}{X_{1}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}})^{-1}{X_{1}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}$ . By Lemma F.4 and Assumption 2, there exists $B_{2}>0$ s.t. $\lVert P_{1}^{\bot}\hat{\beta}_{\textup{II}}\rVert_{2}\leq B_{2}\lVert{X_{1}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}P_{1}^{\bot}\hat{\beta}_{\textup{II}}\rVert_{2}=B_{2}\lVert{X_{1}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\hat{\beta}_{\textup{II}}\rVert_{2}$ . From here, we can follow the exact same steps as those of Lemma 3.2 of Bayati and Montanari [32] to prove our Lemma E.1.

$$ \displaystyle\mathop{\mathrm{plim}}_{p}\frac{1}{p}(v_{\textup{II}}^{i})^{\top}v_{\textup{II}}^{j}= \displaystyle(1-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}})^{2}\mathbb{E}[W_{1}^{2}]+ \displaystyle\kappa_{1}\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\Big[(\beta_{1}-\xi(\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}Z_{\textup{II}}^{i-1},\eta(Z^{t_{0}+i-1}_{1},\cdots,Z^{t_{0}+i-1}_{E}))-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}(\beta_{1}-\eta(Z^{t_{0}+i-1}_{1},\cdots,Z^{t_{0}+i-1}_{E}))) \displaystyle\Sigma_{1}(\beta_{1}-\xi(\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}Z_{\textup{II}}^{j-1},\eta(Z^{t_{0}+i-1}_{1},\cdots,Z^{t_{0}+i-1}_{E}))-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}(\beta_{1}-\eta(Z^{t_{0}+i-1}_{1},\cdots,Z^{t_{0}+i-1}_{E})))\Big], \displaystyle\text{where }Z_{\textup{II}}^{i-1}= \displaystyle\zeta^{*}Z_{1}^{t_{0}+i-1}+\sqrt{1-(\zeta^{*})^{2}}(Z_{1}^{\prime})^{i-1} \displaystyle Z_{\textup{II}}^{j-1}= \displaystyle\zeta^{*}Z_{1}^{t_{0}+j-1}+\sqrt{1-(\zeta^{*})^{2}}(Z_{1}^{\prime})^{j-1}. $$

The Gaussian matrix $[Z_{1}^{t_{0}+i-1}|(Z_{1}^{\prime})^{i-1}|Z_{2}^{t_{0}+i-1}|\cdots|Z_{E}^{t_{0}+i-1}|Z_{1}^{t_{0}+j-1}|(Z_{1}^{\prime})^{j-1}|Z_{2}^{t_{0}+j-1}|\cdots|Z_{E}^{t_{0}+j-1}]\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times 2(E+1)}$ has iid rows from some $\mathcal{G}\in\mathcal{N}^{(\epsilon_{H})}$ . Hence Assumption 8 (b) guarantees the above limit is well-defined.

#### E.1.3 Proof of Lemma E.3

We need preparation before showing Lemma E.3. Firstly, we present Lemma E.8, which implies the matrix $\Sigma_{(V,\textup{II})}$ from Definition E.3 is well-defined and its elements converge to 1 in the lower-right direction.

#### Lemma E.8.

The function $H_{\textup{II}}:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}$ defined in Assumption 8 (b) is increasing and strictly convex in $\rho\in[0,1]$ . Moreover, $0\leq\frac{\mathrm{d}H_{\textup{II}}}{\mathrm{d}\rho}\leq\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{II}}[1-(\zeta^{*})^{2}]$ , and $(\zeta^{*})^{2}\leq H_{\textup{II}}(0)\leq H_{\textup{II}}(1)=1$ .

#### Proof of Lemma E.8.

The first half of Lemma E.8 follows the same argument as that of our Lemma C.7, or the Lemma C.1 of Bayati and Montanari [32], or the Lemma C.2 of Donoho and Montanari [33]. In our case, for any $p$ , we can re-express $H^{(p)}_{\textup{II}}$ with a function $\nu:\mathbb{R}^{p}\to\mathbb{R}^{p}$ :

$$ \displaystyle H_{\textup{II}}^{(p)}(\rho)= \displaystyle~\frac{(1-\kappa_{1}\,\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}})^{2}\mathbb{E}[W_{1}^{2}]}{(\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*})^{2}}+\frac{\kappa_{1}}{(\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*})^{2}p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbb{E}\left[\nu\left(\sqrt{\rho}Z_{1}^{\prime}+\sqrt{1-\rho}Z_{1}^{\prime\prime}\right)^{{\top}}\nu\left(\sqrt{\rho}Z_{1}^{\prime}+\sqrt{1-\rho}Z_{1}^{\prime\prime\prime}\right)\middle|Z_{1},Z_{2},\cdots,Z_{E}\right]\right], \displaystyle\nu(\cdot)= \displaystyle~\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\left\{\left[\beta_{1}-\xi\left(\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}\cdot\left[\zeta^{*}Z_{1}/\tau^{*}_{1}+\sqrt{1-(\zeta^{*})^{2}}(\,\cdot\,)\right],\,\overline{\eta}\right)-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}(\beta_{1}-\overline{\eta})\right]\right\}, $$

where $\overline{\eta}=\eta(Z_{1},\cdots,Z_{E})$ , $Z_{1},\cdots,Z_{E},Z_{1}^{\prime},Z_{1}^{\prime\prime},Z_{1}^{\prime\prime\prime}$ are independent Gaussian vectors in $R^{p}$ , $Z_{e}\sim N(0,(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}I_{p})$ , $Z_{1}^{\prime},Z_{1}^{\prime\prime},Z_{1}^{\prime\prime\prime}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{iid}}}{{\sim}}N(0,I_{p})$ .

We introduce a total of $p$ iid stationary Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes with covariance function $\exp\left(-t\right)$ , stacked as a vector $X_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{p}$ , then

$$ H_{\textup{II}}^{(p)}=\frac{(1-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}})^{2}\mathbb{E}[W_{1}^{2}]}{(\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*})^{2}}+\frac{\kappa_{1}}{(\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*})^{2}p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbb{E}\left[\nu(X_{0})^{{\top}}\nu(X_{t})\middle|Z_{1},\cdots,Z_{E}\right]\right] $$

with $t=\log(1/\rho)$ . With the same eigen-decomposition trick as that of Lemma C.1 of Bayati and Montanari [32], or Lemma C.2 of Donoho and Montanari [33], we can show $H_{\textup{II}}^{{(p)}}$ is increasing and strictly convex in $\rho\in[0,1]$ , and thus so is $H_{\textup{II}}$ . We have proved the first half of Lemma E.8.

$H_{\textup{II}}(1)=1$ follows from the first equation in Assumption 8 (a). As a sufficient condition of $0\leq\frac{\mathrm{d}H_{\textup{II}}}{\mathrm{d}\rho}\leq\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{II}}[1-(\zeta^{*})^{2}]$ , we prove $\frac{\mathrm{d}H_{\textup{II}}}{\mathrm{d}\rho}(1)=\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{II}}[1-(\zeta^{*})^{2}]$ .

We first compute the partial derivatives at general $\rho\in[0,1]$ , and then set $\rho=1$ . Supposing the limit can be exchanged with the partial derivative, we have

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{d}H_{\textup{II}}}{\mathrm{d}\rho}= \displaystyle\frac{-\kappa_{1}\sqrt{1-(\zeta^{*})^{2}}}{\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}}\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[(\beta_{1}-\overline{\xi}_{(2)}-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{1}(\beta_{1}-\overline{\eta}))^{{\top}}\Sigma_{1}J_{1}(\overline{\xi}_{(1)})\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\rho}}Z_{1}^{\prime}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-\rho}}Z_{1}^{\prime\prime}\right)\right], $$

where we have used the exchangeability of $\overline{\xi}_{(1)}$ and $\overline{\xi}_{(2)}$ to simplify the form. The notation ‘ $J_{1}(\overline{\xi}_{(1)})$ ’ means the $p$ -by- $p$ Jacobian matrix of $\overline{\xi}_{(1)}$ w.r.t. its very first argument from Equation (24). We then invoke Stein’s Lemma:

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{d}H_{\textup{II}}}{\mathrm{d}\rho}= \displaystyle\frac{-\kappa_{1}\sqrt{1-(\zeta^{*})^{2}}}{\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}\sqrt{\rho}}\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[(\beta_{1}-\overline{\xi}_{(2)}-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{1}(\beta_{1}-\overline{\eta}))^{{\top}}\Sigma_{1}J_{1}(\overline{\xi}_{(1)})Z_{1}^{\prime}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\kappa_{1}[1-(\zeta^{*})^{2}]\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\left(J_{1}(\overline{\xi}_{(2)})^{{\top}}\Sigma_{1}J_{1}(\overline{\xi}_{(1)})\right)\right]. $$

When $\rho=1$ , $\overline{\xi}_{(1)}=\overline{\xi}_{(2)}=\overline{\xi}$ . For either $S_{\textup{II}}=\mathrm{supp}(\overline{\xi}-\overline{\eta})$ in the case of $\mu_{\textup{II}}=\mu_{\mathrm{joint}}$ , or $S_{\textup{II}}=\mathrm{supp}(\overline{\xi})$ in the case of $\mu_{\textup{II}}=\mu_{\mathrm{ada}}$ , we have $[J_{1}(\overline{\xi})]_{S^{c}_{\textup{II}}}=0$ , so

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{d}H_{\textup{II}}}{\mathrm{d}\rho}= \displaystyle\kappa_{1}[1-(\zeta^{*})^{2}]\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\left((J_{1}(\overline{\xi}_{(2)})_{S_{\textup{II}}})^{{\top}}(\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},S_{\textup{II}}}(J_{1}(\overline{\xi}_{(1)}))_{S_{\textup{II}}}\right)\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\kappa_{1}[1-(\zeta^{*})^{2}]\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}\left((\Sigma_{1}^{1/2})_{\cdot,S_{\textup{II}}}[(\Sigma_{1})_{S_{\textup{II}},S_{\textup{II}}}]^{-1}(\Sigma_{1}^{1/2})_{S_{\textup{II}},\cdot}\right)\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{II}}[1-(\zeta^{*})^{2}], $$

where the second and third equalities have both used Equation (B-8) for the joint estimator, or Equation (B-10) for the adaptively weighted estimator.

Finally we prove $(\zeta^{*})^{2}\leq H_{\textup{II}}(0)\leq H_{\textup{II}}(1)$ . The side of $H_{\textup{II}}(0)\leq H_{\textup{II}}(1)$ has been argued and follows from the definition of $(\tau^{*}_{\textup{II}})^{2}$ in Assumption 8 (a). For the rest of the claim, recall that we have written $\overline{\eta}=\eta(Z_{1},\cdots,Z_{E})$ , and $\overline{\xi}=\xi(\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}(\zeta^{*}Z_{1}/\tau_{1}^{*}+\sqrt{1-(\zeta^{*})^{2}}Z_{1}^{\prime}),\,\overline{\eta})$ , where $Z_{1},\cdots,Z_{E},Z_{1}^{\prime}$ are independent, $Z_{1}^{\prime}\sim N(0,I_{p})$ . Define $\breve{\xi}=\mathbb{E}[\overline{\xi}|Z_{1},Z_{2},\cdots,Z_{E}]$ . In other words, the integral is taken only w.r.t. $Z_{1}^{\prime}$ . After some algebra, we have

$$ \displaystyle(\tau_{1}^{*}\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*})^{2}H_{\textup{II}}(0)= \displaystyle(1-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}})^{2}\mathbb{E}[W_{1}^{2}]^{2}+\kappa_{1}\mathbb{E}[W_{1}^{2}]\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\left(\beta_{1}-\breve{\xi}-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}(\beta_{1}-\overline{\eta})\right)\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right] \displaystyle+\kappa_{1}^{2}\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\left(\beta_{1}-\breve{\xi}-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}(\beta_{1}-\overline{\eta})\right)\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right]\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\left(\beta_{1}-\overline{\eta}\right)\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right] \displaystyle+\kappa_{1}(1-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}})^{2}\mathbb{E}[W_{1}^{2}]\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\left(\beta_{1}-\overline{\eta}\right)\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right], $$

$$ \displaystyle(\tau_{1}^{*}\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*})^{2}H_{\textup{II}}(1)= \displaystyle(1-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}})^{2}\mathbb{E}[W_{1}^{2}]^{2}+\kappa_{1}\mathbb{E}[W_{1}^{2}]\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\left(\beta_{1}-\overline{\xi}-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}(\beta_{E}-\overline{\eta})\right)\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right] \displaystyle+\kappa_{1}^{2}\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\left(\beta_{1}-\overline{\xi}-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}(\beta_{1}-\overline{\eta})\right)\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right]\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\left(\beta_{1}-\overline{\eta}\right)\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right] \displaystyle+\kappa_{1}(1-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}})^{2}\mathbb{E}[W_{1}^{2}]\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\left\lVert\Sigma_{1}^{1/2}\left(\beta_{1}-\overline{\eta}\right)\right\rVert_{2}^{2}\right], $$

$$ \displaystyle(\tau_{1}^{*}\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}\zeta^{*})^{2}= \displaystyle(1-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}})^{2}\mathbb{E}[W_{1}^{2}]^{2}+\kappa_{1}^{2}\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p^{2}}\mathbb{E}\left[(\beta_{1}-\overline{\eta})\Sigma_{1}\left[\beta_{1}-\breve{\xi}-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}(\beta_{1}-\overline{\eta})\right]\right]^{2} \displaystyle+2\kappa_{1}(1-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}})\mathbb{E}[W_{1}^{2}]\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[(\beta_{1}-\overline{\eta})\Sigma_{1}\left[\beta_{1}-\breve{\xi}-\kappa_{1}\overline{\gamma}_{\textup{I}}(\beta_{1}-\overline{\eta})\right]\right]^{2}. $$

By the law of iterated expectations, $H_{\textup{II}}(1)\geq H_{\textup{II}}(0)$ . By Cauchy’s inequality and the AM-GM inequality, we also see the following relationships:

$$ \displaystyle H_{\textup{II}}(0)\geq(\zeta^{*})^{2}; \displaystyle H_{\textup{II}}(0)=(\zeta^{*})^{2}\iff\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\lVert\breve{\xi}-\overline{\eta}\rVert_{2}^{2}\right]=0, \displaystyle H_{\textup{II}}(1)\geq(\zeta^{*})^{2}; \displaystyle H_{\textup{II}}(1)=(\zeta^{*})^{2}\iff\lim_{p}\frac{1}{p}\mathbb{E}\left[\lVert\overline{\xi}-\overline{\eta}\rVert_{2}^{2}\right]=0. $$

This completes the proof of Lemma E.8. ∎

We need yet another lemma before proving Lemma E.3. Lemma E.9 establishes the convergence of $(v_{1}^{t},r_{1}^{t},\eta(v_{1}^{t},\cdots,v_{E}^{t}))$ of Part I of the GLAMP from Definition E.1 towards $(v_{1}^{\infty},r_{1}^{\infty},\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}})$ .

#### Lemma E.9.

In addition to $v_{1}^{\infty}$ and $r_{1}^{\infty}$ , define for any $e\in[E]$

$$ v_{e}^{\infty}=\frac{{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}}(y_{e}-{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}})}{1-\kappa_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}}+\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}(\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}-\beta_{e}),\quad r_{e}^{\infty}=y_{e}-\frac{y_{e}-{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}}{1-\kappa_{e}\overline{\delta}_{e}}. $$

$\forall\,\epsilon>0$ , $\exists\,T_{0}$ , s.t. $\forall\,t_{0}\geq T_{0},\,t\in\mathbb{N},\,e\in[E]$ , $\lim_{p\to\infty}\mathbb{P}[\frac{1}{p}\lVert\eta(v_{1}^{t+t_{0}},\cdots,v_{E}^{t+t_{0}})-\hat{\beta}_{\mathrm{stack}}\rVert_{2}^{2}<\epsilon]=1$ , and

$$ \displaystyle\lim_{p\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\bigg[\frac{1}{p}\left\lVert v_{e}^{t+t_{0}}-v_{e}^{\infty}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}<\epsilon\bigg]=1,\ \lim_{p\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\bigg[\frac{1}{n_{e}}\left\lVert r_{e}^{t+t_{0}}-r_{e}^{\infty}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}<\epsilon\bigg]=1. $$

#### Proof of Lemma E.9.

The claim about $\eta(v_{1}^{t+t_{0}},\cdots,v_{E}^{t+t_{0}})$ has been proved in Lemma C.6 and is just revisted here. We focus on the rest of Lemma E.9.

Recall from Lemma C.3 that for any $\epsilon>0$ , there exists $T_{0}$ s.t. $\forall\,j>i\geq T_{0},\,\forall\,e\in[E]$ , $\lim_{p}\mathbb{P}[\frac{1}{p}\lVert v_{e}^{i}-v_{e}^{j}\rVert_{2}^{2}<\epsilon]=1$ and $\lim_{p}\mathbb{P}[\frac{1}{n_{e}}\lVert r_{e}^{i}-r_{e}^{j}\rVert_{2}^{2}<\epsilon]=1$ . By re-writing the GLAMP iterates from Part I of Definition E.1, we know for $t_{0}\geq T_{0}$ and $t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle y_{e}-r_{e}^{t+t_{0}}= \displaystyle\frac{y_{e}-{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma^{1/2}_{e}\hat{\beta}^{t+t_{0}}}{1-\kappa_{e}\overline{\delta}^{(p)}_{e}}+\frac{\kappa_{e}\overline{\delta}^{(p)}_{e}}{1-\kappa_{e}\overline{\delta}^{(p)}_{e}}(r_{e}^{t+t_{0}}-r_{e}^{t+t_{0}-1}), \displaystyle v_{e}^{t+t_{0}+1}= \displaystyle\frac{{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}}(y_{e}-{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}\Sigma^{1/2}_{e}\eta^{t+t_{0}})}{1-\kappa_{e}\overline{\delta}^{(p)}_{e}}+\frac{\kappa_{e}\overline{\delta}^{(p)}_{e}}{1-\kappa_{e}\overline{\delta}^{(p)}_{e}}{X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}}^{{\top}}(r_{e}^{t+t_{0}}-r_{e}^{t+t_{0}-1})+\Sigma_{e}^{1/2}(\eta^{t+t_{0}}-\beta_{e}), \displaystyle\text{where }\eta^{t+t_{0}}= \displaystyle\eta(v_{1}^{t+t_{0}},\cdots,v_{E}^{t+t_{0}}) $$

Recall that $\overline{\delta}^{(p)}_{e}\to\overline{\delta}_{e}$ , $\lim_{p}\sigma_{\max}({X_{e}^{\mathrm{iid}}})\leq 1+\sqrt{\kappa_{e}}$ a.s. and $\lambda_{\max}(\Sigma_{e})\leq c_{1}$ . As a result, for any $\epsilon>0$ , there exists $T_{0}$ large enough s.t. $\forall\,t_{0}\geq T_{0}$ and $t\in\mathbb{N}$ ,

$$ \lim_{p}\mathbb{P}\left[\frac{1}{n_{e}}\lVert r_{e}^{t+t_{0}}-r_{e}^{\infty}\rVert_{2}^{2}<\epsilon\right]=1,\quad\lim_{p}\mathbb{P}\left[\frac{1}{p}\lVert v_{e}^{t+t_{0}}-v_{e}^{\infty}\rVert_{2}^{2}<\epsilon\right]=1. $$

Thus we have proved Lemma E.9. ∎

#### Lemma E.10.

Fixing $t\in\mathbb{N_{+}}$ , for any sequence of order- $k$ pseudo-Lipschitz functions $\phi:(\mathbb{R}^{p})^{(t+1)\times(E+1)+E}\to\mathbb{R}$ , $k\geq 1$ , define

$$ A=\phi\left(Z_{\textup{II}}^{t},Z_{\textup{II}}^{t-1},\cdots,Z_{\textup{II}}^{1},Z_{\textup{II}}^{0},Z^{t+t_{0}}_{1},\cdots,Z^{t+t_{0}}_{E},Z^{t+t_{0}-1}_{1},\cdots,Z^{t+t_{0}-1}_{E},\cdots,Z^{t_{0}}_{1},\cdots,Z^{t_{0}}_{E},\beta_{1},\beta_{2},\cdots,\beta_{E}\right), $$

where the Gaussian variables on the right hand side are exactly from the limit in Lemma E.2. We define another quantity $B$ :

$$ B=\phi\left(Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{t},Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{t-1},\cdots,Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{1},Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{0},Z_{1},\cdots,Z_{E},Z_{1},\cdots,Z_{E},\cdots,Z_{1},\cdots,Z_{E},\beta_{1},\beta_{2},\cdots,\beta_{E}\right), $$

where (i) $\forall\,0\leq i\leq t$ , $Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{i}=\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}\zeta^{*}(Z_{1}/\tau_{E}^{*})+\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}\sqrt{1-(\zeta^{*})}Z_{1,\infty}^{i}$ ; (ii) $Z_{e}\sim N(0,(\tau_{e}^{*})^{2}I_{p})$ for $e\in[E]$ , (iii) The Gaussian matrix $[Z_{1,\infty}^{0}|Z_{E,\infty}^{1}|\cdots|Z_{E,\infty}^{t}]\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times(t+1)}$ is independent of $\{Z_{1},Z_{2},\cdots,Z_{E}\}$ , and has iid rows drawn from $N(0,\Sigma_{V,\textup{II}}^{t})$ . Then we have

$$ \lim_{t_{0}\to\infty}\sup_{p\geq 1}\left\lvert E[A]-E[B]\right\rvert=0. $$

#### Proof of Lemma E.10.

If we write the Gaussian variables used by $A$ and $B$ into matrices $Z_{A},Z_{B}\in\mathbb{R}^{(p\times(t+1)(E+1))}$ :

$$ \displaystyle Z_{A}= \displaystyle[Z_{\textup{II}}^{t}|Z_{\textup{II}}^{t-1}|\cdots|Z_{\textup{II}}^{1}|Z_{\textup{II}}^{0}|Z^{t+t_{0}}_{1}|\cdots|Z^{t+t_{0}}_{E}|Z^{t+t_{0}-1}_{1}|\cdots|Z^{t+t_{0}-1}_{E}|\cdots|Z^{t_{0}}_{1}|\cdots|Z^{t_{0}}_{E}], \displaystyle Z_{B}= \displaystyle[Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{t}|Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{t-1}|\cdots|Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{1}|Z_{{\textup{II},\infty}}^{0}|Z_{1}|\cdots|Z_{E}|Z_{1}|\cdots|Z_{E}|\cdots|Z_{1}|\cdots|Z_{E}]. $$

Then by the definitions of the Gaussian variables from Lemma E.2 and Lemma E.10, we know both $Z_{A}$ and $Z_{B}$ have iid rows drawn from some $(t+1)(E+1)$ -dimensional Gaussian distribution, with mean zero and covariance matrices $\Sigma_{A}$ and $\Sigma_{B}$ . Both covariance matrices are $(t+1)(E+1)$ -dimensional and do not depend on $p$ .

We first show $\lim_{t_{0}\to\infty}\lVert\Sigma_{A}-\Sigma_{B}\rVert_{2}=0$ .

By definition, $\Sigma_{B}\in\mathbb{R}^{(t+1)(E+1)\times(t+1)(E+1)}$ do not depend on $t_{0}$ . On the other hand for $\Sigma_{A}$ , by Lemma C.3, $\lim_{t_{0}\to\infty}\sup_{j>i\geq 0,e\in[E]}\rho^{t_{0}+i,t_{0}+j}_{e}=1$ . Among different environments, we know for different $e\in[E]$ , $\{[Z_{e}^{t+t_{0}}|Z_{e}^{t+t_{0}-1}|\cdots|Z_{e}^{t_{0}}]:e\in[E]\}$ are independent Gaussian matrices. As a result, we have proved that for the lower-right sub-blocks:

$$ \lim_{t_{0}\to\infty}(\Sigma_{A})_{(t+2):(t+1)(E+1),\,(t+2):(t+1)(E+1)}=(\Sigma_{B})_{(t+2):(t+1)(E+1),\,(t+2):(t+1)(E+1)}. $$

For the first $(t+1)$ rows of $Z_{A}$ , we know from Lemma E.2 that $Z_{\textup{II}}^{i}=\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}\zeta^{*}Z_{1}^{t_{0}+i}/\tau_{1}^{*}+\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}\sqrt{1-(\zeta^{*})^{2}}(Z_{1}^{\prime})^{i}$ for some $(Z_{1}^{\prime})^{i}\mathchoice{\mathrel{\hbox to0.0pt{$\displaystyle\perp$\hss}\mkern 2.0mu{\displaystyle\perp}}}{\mathrel{\hbox to0.0pt{$\textstyle\perp$\hss}\mkern 2.0mu{\textstyle\perp}}}{\mathrel{\hbox to0.0pt{$\scriptstyle\perp$\hss}\mkern 2.0mu{\scriptstyle\perp}}}{\mathrel{\hbox to0.0pt{$\scriptscriptstyle\perp$\hss}\mkern 2.0mu{\scriptscriptstyle\perp}}}Z_{1}^{t_{0}+i}$ , $\forall\,0\leq i\leq t$ . For convenience, we apply a linear transformation to $Z_{A}$ , take an excerpt at two time steps $0\leq i<j\leq t$ , and consider the Gaussian matrix $[\frac{1}{\tau_{1}^{*}}Z_{1}^{i+t_{0}}|(Z_{1}^{\prime})^{i}|\frac{1}{\tau_{2}^{*}}Z_{2}^{i+t_{0}}|\cdots|\frac{1}{\tau_{E}^{*}}Z_{E}^{i+t_{0}}|\frac{1}{\tau_{1}^{*}}Z_{1}^{j+t_{0}}|(Z_{1}^{\prime})^{j}|\frac{1}{\tau_{2}^{*}}Z_{2}^{j+t_{0}}|\cdots|\frac{1}{\tau_{E}^{*}}Z_{E}^{j+t_{0}}]\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times 2(E+1)}$ . Each row of it follows a $2(E+1)$ -dimensional Gaussian distribution, which we denote as $\mathcal{G}^{i,j}$ .

We focus on the correlation between the two elements in each iid row of $[(Z_{1}^{\prime})^{i}|(Z_{1}^{\prime})^{j}]\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times 2}$ , which we denote as $\varrho^{i,j}$ . We want to show $\lim_{t_{0}to\infty}\varrho^{i,j}=(\Sigma_{(V,\textup{II})})_{i,j}$ , and then the upper-left block of $\Sigma_{A}$ will also converge to that of $\Sigma_{B}$ . This is because for columns of $B$ , $Z_{\textup{II}}^{i}=\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}\zeta^{*}Z_{1}/\tau_{1}^{*}+\tau_{\textup{II}}^{*}\sqrt{1-(\zeta^{*})^{2}}Z^{i}_{1,\infty}$ and $[Z^{0}_{1,\infty}|Z^{1}_{1,\infty}|\cdots|Z^{t}_{1,\infty}]$ has iid rows from $N(0,\Sigma_{(V,\textup{II})}^{t})$ by construction.

When $i\geq 1$ , $\varrho^{i,j}=H_{\textup{II}}^{\epsilon_{H}}(\mathcal{G}^{i-1.j-1})$ . This is because of the GLAMP convergence in Lemma E.2.
